rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the goal is to establish a strong, well-motivated multimodal baseline that reduces uncertainty about the core design space. config_004 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) uses two well-established encoders (scVI for scRNA-seq, ResNet50 for images) combined with a principled multi-profile aggregation (transformer) and a simple, interpretable fusion (weighted). This configuration sits near the 'center of mass' of the design space: it is complex enough to be competitive but relies on robust, validated components so that any failure signals a structural issue rather than an encoder choice. Performance here gives a strong reference point: if it is competitive, subsequent experiments can explore scgpt/ViT-L upgrades and alternative fusion; if it underperforms, I can ablate to identify whether multiprofile+transformer or the specific encoder pair is the bottleneck. With 9 experiments remaining, this single informative anchor maximally guides the next 9 choices.

Evidence: config_004 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) achieved 71.3% accuracy / 69.5% F1, establishing a working multimodal baseline. Uncertainty: it is unclear whether the relatively modest ResNet50 image encoder is a bottleneck compared to the more powerful ImageNet-pretrained ViT-L. This experiment (config_033) makes a single clean change—swapping image_encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l—while holding the RNA encoder (scvi_n200), aggregation (transformer), fusion (weighted), and profile setting (multiprofile) constant. This directly tests whether a stronger visual backbone translates into higher validation accuracy within the same architectural framework. It is the best use of experiment 2 because: (1) it is a minimal, interpretable ablation that isolates one high-impact variable, (2) if ViT-L helps, it unlocks a family of promising configs (017, 042, 051, etc.) for the remaining 8 experiments, and (3) with only one prior data point, a targeted exploitation of the proven architecture is more informative than a broad exploration or a baseline that would not change the multimodal search trajectory.

Evidence: The two completed experiments (config_004 and config_033) differ only in image encoder (resnet50 vs imagenet_vit_l), with ViT giving ~1.2% higher accuracy (0.725 vs 0.713) but slightly lower F1. Both use scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder, so we have zero information about whether a different RNA encoder (scgpt) could improve performance with the best image encoder. Question: Does scgpt, a generative RNA encoder with a different inductive bias than the variational scvi_n200, complement the ViT image features better or worse under the same transformer+weighted fusion setup? Why this is the best next step: With only 2 data points and both sharing the same RNA encoder, the RNA encoder dimension is completely unexplored. Testing scgpt with the best-performing image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) and the same aggregation/fusion (transformer/weighted) isolates the RNA encoder effect. If scgpt improves accuracy, it opens a high-value direction for the remaining 7 experiments; if not, we confirm scvi_n200 is the right choice and can focus exploitation on fusion/aggregation variations. This is the highest-information experiment to reduce uncertainty on a core design axis.

The current best is config_033 (scvi_n200 + ViT-L + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725). Evidence strongly favors scvi_n200 over scgpt (~20pt gap) and ViT-L over ResNet50 (~1.2pt gain). The key remaining uncertainty within this promising direction is the fusion strategy: weighted vs. concat. Config_017 is a clean single-variable ablation of config_033 (only fusion changes from weighted to concat), isolating whether the learned weighted combination adds value over simple concatenation. This is the best use of the next slot because it directly exploits the strongest configuration while resolving a high-impact design question, and with 6 experiments remaining, we can then test aggregation (avgpool vs. transformer) and profile setting in subsequent runs.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_033 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725), with config_017 (same but concat fusion, acc=0.721) close behind. Both use transformer aggregation. scvi_n200 clearly dominates scgpt (0.725 vs 0.520), and imagenet_vit_l edges out resnet50. Uncertainty: It is unclear whether the transformer aggregation is genuinely contributing to performance or whether a simpler avgpool aggregation would perform comparably, which would simplify the architecture without cost. This experiment (config_042: scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) directly tests aggregation method while holding the best encoder and fusion choices constant. If avgpool matches transformer, we gain architectural simplicity; if it falls short, we confirm transformer's value and can focus remaining budget on other levers (e.g., singleprofile vs multiprofile or fusion tuning). This is the highest-information single test given 5 remaining experiments.

Evidence: All 5 completed experiments used multiprofile, and the current best (config_033: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725) is multiprofile. The only major untested architectural dimension is profile_setting. Question: config_021 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l, singleprofile, weighted) directly tests whether the multiprofile + transformer aggregation complexity is actually contributing to performance or whether a simpler singleprofile pipeline with the same strong encoders is competitive. Why this is the best next experiment: With 4 experiments remaining, resolving this fundamental design choice is high-value. If singleprofile matches or beats 0.725, it opens a simpler, potentially more tunable path. If it falls short, it confirms multiprofile + transformer is essential and the remaining budget should focus on fine-tuning within that space (e.g., fusion or aggregation variants). This reduces the largest remaining uncertainty before committing the final experiments to exploitation.

Evidence: The best config (config_033, acc=0.7250) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted + multiprofile. scgpt was clearly inferior (0.520), and scvi_n200 consistently outperforms across tested settings. However, pca_n2000 has never been tested in the optimal multimodal configuration space. This experiment (config_011: pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted + multiprofile) is a clean single-variable swap of the RNA encoder, isolating whether the learned scvi representation is truly necessary or whether a simpler linear PCA projection suffices. If pca_n2000 is competitive, it confirms the bottleneck is elsewhere and frees future experiments to explore other dimensions; if it is substantially worse, it firmly validates scvi_n200 and lets us focus the remaining 3 experiments on confirming the best config's robustness or testing marginal variants. With only 3 experiments left after this one, reducing uncertainty on the most impactful untested variable (RNA encoder) in the top-performing configuration is the highest-value use of this slot.

Evidence: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile is clearly the best sub-space (0.725 for transformer+weighted, 0.721 for transformer+concat, 0.706 for avgpool+weighted). The only untested combination in this top sub-space is avgpool+concat (config_051). This experiment completes the 2×2 aggregation×fusion grid for the best encoder pair, clarifying whether there is a non-additive interaction that could unexpectedly boost performance. While unlikely to surpass 0.725, it is the most informative remaining test within the proven-best architecture family. With only 2 experiments left after this, confirming the interaction structure (or ruling out a surprise) is the best use of budget before finalizing the winner as config_033.

The best config so far (config_033: scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, 0.725) has all four of its direct single-parameter neighbors already tested (transformer+concat=0.721, avgpool+weighted=0.706, avgpool+concat=0.715, resnet50+transformer+weighted=0.713). The only remaining untested variant in the high-performing scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer region is config_024 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + transformer + concat). While resnet50 is ~1.2% below vit_l and concat is ~0.4% below weighted for transformer aggregation, this experiment tests whether the interaction of concat fusion with transformer aggregation on the weaker image encoder produces any unexpected synergy. Given that only 1 experiment remains after this one and all other untested configurations involve clearly inferior components (scgpt, pca_n2000, singleprofile, or unimodal baselines), config_024 is the highest-probability candidate to approach or exceed the current best, and it provides the most informative data point to guide the final experiment.

The current best is config_033 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.725), and all four aggregation×fusion combinations for that exact encoder pair have been tested. The strongest remaining untested combination uses the proven-best RNA encoder (scvi_n200), multiprofile setting, and weighted fusion (which showed a particularly large advantage over concat for resnet50: 0.713 vs 0.688), paired with the second-best image encoder (resnet50) and avgpool aggregation. While unlikely to surpass 0.725, config_048 represents the highest-prior untested configuration given the evidence: weighted fusion is critical for resnet50, and this is the last experiment in the budget, so exploiting the most validated component choices in an untested pairing is the most rational final probe.
